question.text: Capital gains bonds issued by entities such as NHAI, NABARD, National Housing Bank, and other specifically notified entities allow investors to claim long-term capital gains tax saving under __________ of the Income Tax Act, 1961.

explanation.text: The Logic: Under Section 54EC of the Income Tax Act, 1961, long-term capital gains tax saving is available through investment in capital gains bonds issued by NHAI, NABARD, National Housing Bank, and other specifically notified entities, as referenced in the NISM XII workbook. The Trap: Section 80C provides deductions for investments in PPF, ELSS, etc. -- it is the most commonly known tax-saving section but does not cover capital gains reinvestment. Section 10(15) provides interest income exemptions. Section 88 was an old rebate provision that has been discontinued. Note: The workbook references Section 54EC capital gains bonds issued by NHAI, NABARD, NHB, and specifically notified entities (NISM XII page 50).
